newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Norilsk Nickel union official found dead.
newsitem.headline: Russian Norilsk Nickel union official found dead.

text.p: A senior Norilsk Nickel trade union official apparently died in a fall from a Moscow hotel window after attending the Russian mining and smelting company's annual shareholders' meeting, a police official said on Monday.

Norilsk spokesman Sergei Vetchinin said that Boris Degtyaryov, deputy chairman of the United Trade Union Committee at Norilsk's flagship plant, was found dead on Saturday under his hotel window. He had no further details.
A federal police spokesman said the incident was being treated as suicide and declined to comment further.
Degtyaryov had been in Moscow for Norilsk's shareholders' meeting on Friday.

His union was a force in mobilising workers at Norilsk's flagship plant, known as the Norilsk mining and metallurgical complex, in a dispute in March and April over unpaid wages. A strike threat was dropped after the union and management reached agreement.
Financially-troubled RAO Norilsky Nikel, the parent company of the complex, is one of the world's top producers of nickel and platinum group metals.
The group is struggling to implement a restructuring programme aimed at reducing tax debts and trimming its vast social infrastructure costs.
